wayfaring._doc: On the road (Systems/Wayfaring.cs). Each hero in a party takes one day job, in 'order', the free hero best at the job's skill first: navigate (hard country, harder the slower it is: 'slowDc' a unit of slowness), forage (after 'rations' nights out) and track (the way into the site). The night jobs, keeping watch and treating wounds on a rest, go to whoever is best at them. A job is routine, and nobody rolls, when 10 + the bonus meets the DC. A lost navigator costs 'lost' of the stretch's hours (at least 'lostMin'); a hungry night costs 1 on every blow and check until a meal; a tracker who finds the way in spares them the first room.

navigate.name: Navigator
navigate.why: Survival finds the way through hard country; a lost navigator costs hours.

watch.name: Watch
watch.why: Perception at night spots trouble coming for the camp.

treat.name: Medic
treat.why: Medicine on a short rest gives back extra hit points.

forage.name: Forager
forage.why: Survival feeds the party once the rations run out; hungry heroes fight worse.

track.name: Tracker
track.why: Survival reads the signs to a back way in, past the first room.

lost: {name} loses the way in {feature}, and it costs them {days}.
In {feature} every trail looks the same; {name} has them walking in circles for {days}.
{name} is sure of the way through {feature} until the same dead tree comes round twice: {days} lost.
found: {name} reads the ground in {feature} and keeps them on the right line.
{name} finds the old way through {feature} by the moss on the stones.
hungry: The last of the rations went yesterday. They go to sleep hungry.
Nothing in the pot tonight but water and hope.
hungryForager: {name} comes back to camp empty-handed: there is nothing to eat out here.
{name} forages till dark and finds only roots nobody can stomach.
fed: {name} comes back with a brace of hares, and the pot bubbles.
{name} finds berries, mushrooms and a stream full of trout.
herbs: {name} finds a patch of healing herbs as well, and brews a draught for the road.
treated: {name} cleans and stitches the worst of the wounds ({hp} more hit points between them).
{name} sets a splint and binds the cuts, and everyone feels the better for it ({hp} hp).
tracked: {name} reads the tracks round to a back way in, past the first of the guards.
{name} finds where the creatures come and go, and leads them in by a gap nobody watches.
untracked: {name} loses the tracks in the stony ground, and they go in by the front.

wonders._doc: Strange places that bend the rules, placed on their own dice after the rest of the world: 'perRing' per ring from ring 'rings'[0] to [1], each a kind from roads.json kinds with a 'wonder'. Oases go only in the themes the kind names; a 'ferry' wonder takes over one lake.

gateways._doc: Old gateways in the wilds that link two far places. A known, open gateway saves days when it lies near the way; a 'riddle' lock opens to a party's best Investigation against 'riddleDc' and stays open; a 'password' lock opens when an allied people living near either end tells the word. Parties learn of a gateway passing within 'notice' days of an end.

through: They step through {gate} and out under another sky, days nearer.
{gate} hums as they pass under it; the far arch stands in country a week's walk off.
riddle: {name} works out the riddle carved over {gate} ({roll}), and the arch fills with light. It will open for anyone now.
riddleFailed: {name} puzzles over the riddle on {gate} ({roll}) and gets nowhere. They walk.
learned: The {people} tell the council the word that opens {gate}. Companies can use it now.
An elder of the {people} whispers the old word for {gate}. It is open to the town's companies.
found: Returning companies tell of {gate}, an old arch in the wilds that leads somewhere far away.

bridges._doc: Rope bridges over gorges (Systems/Bridges.cs): raiders of a live lair in the same country, out to ring 'ring', cut them now and then; the town rebuilds a cut one in stone for 'stone' gold.

texts.cut: Raiders out of {site} cut {bridge} over {gorge}. It hangs from one side now, and companies must go round.
texts.stone: Masons rebuild {bridge} over {gorge} in stone. No raider will cut it again.

crossBold: {leader} will not hear of the long way round: they go straight {through} {name}.
crossHurry: With people waiting on them, they take the quick way {through} {name}.
There is no time to go around; they cut {through} {name}.
cross: They talk it over at the edge of {name} and decide to chance the way {through}.
The way round {name} would cost them {days}; they go {through}.
skirt: They give {name} a wide berth and take the long way round, a detour of {days}.
{leader} wants no part of {name}; they go around it, {days} out of their way.
skirtWounded: Hurt as they are, nobody wants to risk {name} again; they limp the long way round ({days} more).
They carry their wounded around {name} rather than through it, {days} the longer.
skirtOverruled: {bold} wants to cut {through} {name}, but the others outvote them and they take the long way round ({days} more).
shortRest: They stop for an hour to catch their breath and bind their wounds.
A short rest in a quiet corner: water, bandages, a whetstone.
shortRestInterrupted: Their rest is cut short: something has heard them.
camp: They make camp for the night and post a watch.
A cold camp under the stars, a watch kept in turns.
campAmbush: Deep in the night, {watcher} on watch hears movement beyond the firelight.
Something comes for their camp in the dark; {watcher} raises the alarm.
campSurprised: Something comes for their camp in the dark, and {watcher}, on watch, has nodded off.
campBefore: They reach {site} late in the day and camp out of sight to go in at first light, rested.
fallBack: They fall back out of {site}, find a hollow a safe distance off and sleep the long sleep of the exhausted.
They pull back to a ruined wall a mile off, light no fire, and rest until they can fight again.
tryAgain: Rested and healed, they go back in to finish what they started. {site} is ready for them this time.
At first light they try again. The defenders have had time to prepare too.
giveUp: Twice beaten, they know when the place is beyond them.

ranges._doc: Mountain walls between the far rings, broken only at passes: at sites in their line and a few more (Roads.Ranges). Days but arc in degrees.

peril.name: the avalanche
text: Snow cracks like a thunderclap above them and the whole slope starts to move.
A shelf of rock and snow lets go over the pass and comes down on them.
peril.win: They ride it out, dig each other free and go on, shaken.
peril.lose: When the snow settles their packs are somewhere under it.

kinds.name: ridge

text: a rockslide on the high pass
a blizzard rolls over the saddle
a ledge gives way under their boots

ambushText: something with wings and claws drops on them from the crags
a band of raiders lying in wait at the top of the pass

peril.name: the sucking mud
text: The ground under them turns to soup and starts to swallow them whole.
The bog takes the first of them to the chest, then the next.
peril.win: Roped together, they haul each other out onto firm ground.
peril.lose: They get out, but the mire keeps their packs and half their boots.

kinds.name: mire

text: sucking mud to the waist
a fever off the stagnant water
leeches the size of a hand

ambushText: the water stirs and something rises out of it
eyes in the reeds, then teeth

peril.name: the wildfire
text: Smoke on the wind, then the roar: the wood is burning and the fire is coming their way.
A dry summer, a lightning strike, and the whole wood goes up around them.
peril.win: They find a stream and run down it ahead of the flames.
peril.lose: They come out of the smoke blistered and coughing, barely.

kinds.name: deep wood

text: they lose the path among the briars
a deadfall rigged across a game trail
a stinging cloud of spores from a rotten log

ambushText: shapes move between the trees, keeping pace with them
a hunting pack picks up their scent

peril.name: the cliff climb
text: The way down the gorge wall is a crumbling chimney of rock and old pitons.
The path along the gorge has fallen away, and the only way on is the cliff face.
peril.win: Hand over hand, with a rope belayed round every outcrop, they make it.
peril.lose: A hold breaks; the rope saves a life but not much skin.

kinds.name: gorge

text: a rope bridge sways and a plank snaps
they climb down one wall and up the other
the ford at the bottom runs white and fast

ambushText: something lairs under the bridge
rocks come down from above, thrown by someone

kinds.name: haunted ground

text: a chill that settles in the bones and will not leave
voices on the wind that call them by name
a grave mist that steals the breath

ambushText: the dead do not lie quiet here
a barrow door stands open, and something walks out of it

peril.name: the sandstorm
text: A brown wall rises on the horizon and comes on faster than a horse.
The wind gets up, the sky goes the colour of rust, and the storm swallows them.
peril.win: They shelter behind the beasts and a dune's lee, and dig out when it passes.
peril.lose: The storm scours away their water skins and half their kit.

kinds.name: badlands

text: the heat and no water
a dust storm that strips the skin
the ground cracks and vents scalding steam

ambushText: something burrows up out of the sand
riders on the horizon, coming fast

peril.name: the whiteout
text: The snow and sky become one white wall, and the crevasses are somewhere in it.
A blizzard comes off the glacier, and every step could be onto nothing.
peril.win: Roped and counting steps, they come out of it the way they meant to go.
peril.lose: Frostbitten and half-buried, they stagger out of it a long way from where they meant.

kinds.name: icefield

text: a crevasse hidden under fresh snow
cold that bites through every layer
a whiteout that turns them in circles

ambushText: white shapes rise out of the snow
a hunter of the ice has been following them

kinds.name: lake

text: a squall sweeps the open water
the cold off the water in their bones

ambushText: something long and pale rises under them
the water's own guardian does not like trespassers

kinds.name: peaks

text: winds off the summits that throw them about
thin air and a long way to fall

ambushText: something nests on the summits and comes down for them
rocs wheel above the peaks

kinds.name: sea

text: a squall off the open sea
a cross-swell that has half of them sick over the side

ambushText: longboats come out of the sea mist
something huge surfaces beside the boat

kinds.name: open sea

text: a gale on the open sea
a calm that leaves them drifting for days
fog so thick the lookout can't see the bow

ambushText: a corsair sail on the horizon, closing
something huge surfaces beside the boat
the reef folk come up over the rail

kinds.name: dead-magic ground

text: no spell will catch here, and the air tastes of old pennies

ambushText: things that hate magic wait in the stillness for casters to stumble in

text: In {name} no magic works: spells die on the lips, and every ward goes dark.
moss-grown stones round a black, deep well
They stop at {name}, and {name2} drops a coin in and makes a wish.
wish: The well hums. {name2}'s wish comes true in its fashion: their wounds close and a purse of old coins lies on the lip ({gold} gold).
boon: Something glints in the bucket: a stoppered vial of something red and warm.
nothing: The coin falls a long way. Nothing happens, or nothing they notice.
curse: The well laughs. {name2} goes cold to the bone, and the luck goes out of them until they're home.

kinds.name: black water

text: a cold mist hangs on the water

ambushText: something in the water follows the boat

text: A skeleton in a boatman's hood poles them over {name} for {toll} gold a head, and says nothing at all.
The bone ferryman of {name} holds out a hand for {toll} gold each, and takes them over without a word.

kinds.name: dragon bones

text: ribs as tall as towers, and a wind that moans through them

ambushText: the bones of the lesser dead get up and come for them
scavengers that nest in a dragon's skull

text: {name2} knows dragon bone from stone, and they cut away a fang worth {gold} gold.
{name2} finds a scale the size of a shield among the ribs ({gold} gold).
missed: The bones are picked clean; whatever was worth taking went with older thieves.

kinds.name: fey ring

text: a ring of white mushrooms, and music very faint

ambushText: the dancers do not like to be interrupted

text: {name2} hears the music and will not let the others dance: they walk round the ring, rested just by its nearness.
They lie down by {name}, and wake whole and rested as if they'd slept a week.
missed: They dance. When they stop, their purses are lighter and their potions drunk, and nobody remembers giving anything away.

text: palms and a pool of clean water
They rest at {name}: shade, dates and clean water. Their skins are full again.
palms and a pool of clean water
{name2} sees the pool breathe, and they give {name} a wide berth. The bones round its edge are not all camels'.
missed: The water is sweet and cold, right up until the pool opens its mouth.

kinds.name: mountain wall

text: a storm on the high wall that throws them against the rock
a cornice gives way under the leader

ambushText: something that nests on the wall drops on them
giants on the heights roll stones down the pass

kinds.name: hunting grounds

text: fresh tracks bigger than a cart wheel
a kill left out as bait

ambushText: the pack has been pacing them for a mile
something big comes out of the long grass
they walk straight into the beasts' feeding ground

kinds.name: monster haunts

text: the bones of the last party to try it
nests in every hollow

ambushText: the hollow they camp in is somebody's lair
a monster's brood boils out of the ground
the ground itself opens its mouth
